data.description: Seed intent (from producer): The existing 'follow on Steam to unlock a game' reward system is a partial implementation. Generalise it so that arbitrary actions on any platform can unlock games in the launcher — e.g. follow on Steam, follow on itch.io, review on WaveDash, wishlist, etc. Reuse the existing game-agnostic bundled-content unlock + persistence mechanism (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC) and align with the unified ContentUnlockStore contract (CG-0MUNW63UL0086J3G).
data.title: Platform-agnostic action unlocks: reward games for arbitrary actions on any platform

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Intake interview — 3 open questions for the producer before the brief can be frozen:

1. **Scope of platform adapters.** Do we build real adapters for Steam follow + itch.io follow + WaveDash review in this item, or generalise the mechanism behind a platform-action interface and ship Steam (existing) plus config-driven stubs, adding further adapters incrementally? *Recommended: generalise + ship one non-Steam proof-of-generality (itch.io follow).*

2. **Verification model for platforms with no public detection API** (itch.io follow, WaveDash review). Options: (a) manual self-attest (honour system) after the action URL opens — same pattern as the existing Steam `claimManually()` fallback; (b) OAuth/API where available and self-attest otherwise; (c) proof submission (URL/screenshot) with manual review. *Recommended: (a) — no new external auth dependency, offline-capable, consistent with the current Steam fallback.*

3. **Architecture: unify with achievement triggers, or keep parallel?** The give-away epic (CG-0MSMGKVSS000ZEDL) is introducing a unified multi-game `ContentUnlockStore` (CG-0MUNW63UL0086J3G). Should platform-action rewards and achievement give-aways share one discriminated `UnlockRule` trigger model (`platform-action` | `achievement`), or stay two siblings over the same store? *Recommended: one unified trigger model — single source of truth for the Game Selector, avoids two parallel engines.*
